attributes.body:
G2 expands Buyer Intent across four software discovery platforms, delivering up to 2x more signals.

June 3, 2026

Table of Contents

G2 research shows that half of B2B software buyers now start their research with AI chatbots - but the buying journey doesn't end there. Even with AI building their shortlists, most buyers are still reading reviews, comparing vendors, and evaluating competitors long before they speak to sales. For revenue teams, that activity goes largely undetected, and deals are increasingly entering the pipeline much later than they should.

G2 Buyer Intent is built around that reality, and I'm excited to share that The G2 has now expanded the experience even further to bring together buyer research activity across G2, Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp into a single unified view. Software vendors now get broader visibility into real software evaluation behavior across the platforms where buyers do their research, all within their existing workflows, at no additional cost.

What's changing with G2 Buyer Intent

This expansion is the direct result of G2's acquisition of Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp (now called G2 Digital Markets) from Gartner in early 2026. G2 Buyer Intent now brings together first-party buyer behavior data from four of the most trusted software research platforms into a single, unified experience. Buyer behavior from the entire G2 family of brands now flows into a single Buyer Intent view, giving teams a more complete picture of in-market account activity that no other intent provider can replicate.

The expanded experience provides broader visibility into real software evaluation behavior, including:

* Reading reviews
* Comparing products and vendors
* Researching competitors
* Viewing category and product pages
* Evaluating software solutions

Early data indicates that customers can gain up to 2x more signals through the expanded dataset, including 36% more accounts actively in-market. Nearly one-third of those signals are brand new, representing buyers who were previously invisible across G2, Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp. The impact will vary by category and buyer behavior patterns, though early results show particularly strong signal growth in regions and industries that previously had limited coverage.

For existing Buyer Intent customers, here's what the expansion means in practice:

* More actionable buyer signals within your existing Buyer Intent workflows, now from all four properties
* More opportunities to identify and engage in-market accounts earlier
* More pipeline potential powered by expanded intent coverage

Adam Smith, Account Executive at Hootsuite, shared his excitement about the opportunity this expanded G2 data set presents:

"Having used G2 Buyer Intent in a past role, I was excited to start using it right away at Hootsuite. Within two months of accessing the data, I closed my first deal sourced from a G2 comparison signal."

Adam Smith
Account Executive, Hootsuite

Adam continued, "Since then, I've enabled our entire AE team on what's become my 'secret' prospecting tool, and they're already seeing an increase in actionable accounts. With the addition of G2 Digital Markets data, we now have even better visibility into in-market buying activity and stronger signals to prioritize the right accounts at the right time."

Teams looking to take data even further can use G2 MCPs, including with Claude and HubSpot, to bring Buyer Intent signals directly into AI-powered tools where revenue teams already work. It's part of a broader effort to make G2 Intent available across the platforms and workflows where decisions actually get made. The G2'll share more on the full MCP roadmap at its Q2 Innovation Drop on June 17.

Why real buyer evaluation behavior matters

Unlike many intent providers that rely on third-party web browsing data and infer purchase intent from general online activity, G2 Buyer Intent is built on first-party data from buyers who are actively researching and evaluating software on G2, Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp. That means reviews being read, vendors being compared, competitors being researched, and categories being explored by buyers who are actually in the market for software, not general web visitors whose browsing gets interpreted as intent.

Broader visibility into real buyer evaluation behavior means:

* More in-market accounts identified earlier in the buying journey
* Better prioritization of outreach and pipeline activity
* Demand captured that would have otherwise gone undetected
* A clearer picture of where buyer evaluation activity is increasing or decreasing across a product portfolio

No new tools, no new cost. Already live.

The expanded Buyer Intent experience is available to existing Buyer Intent customers at no additional cost. There is no additional setup, no new integrations, and nothing to configure. Customers can access expanded signals today in my.G2 under Buyer Activity.

Get started today

Software buying happens across multiple platforms, and revenue teams need visibility across them all to act on demand already in motion. The expanded Buyer Intent experience is live now. Existing customers can log into my.G2 to explore the expanded signals within their current workflows and integrations.

Want to review your Buyer Intent strategy in light of the expanded experience? Connect with the G2 team.

Andrea Youmans is Principal Product Marketing Manager at G2, where she leads go-to-market strategy for buyer intent and data solutions. With a background spanning Outreach, Amazon Web Services, and AT&T. Andrea brings deep expertise in turning complex AI and data products into compelling, customer-first narratives. Her work focuses on helping revenue teams harness intent signals, predictive insights, and generative AI to drive pipeline, accelerate deal velocity, and stay ahead of the competition.

attributes.body:
G2 to acquire Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp from Gartner.

G2, the world's largest and most trusted software marketplace, has inked an agreement to acquire Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp from Gartner, Inc. The combined additions add some of the top B2B software discovery and review platforms onto one ecosystem with the singular focus of facilitating global software buying and selling.

This partnership will enable G2 to integrate its unique user base, data, and user ratings to aid businesses in software discovery, assessment, and purchase. The partnership also promises to produce improved recommendations for software to the buyer, better visibility of the software seller, and a stronger base of a market for software as the use of AI develops and changes the way people search.

"This acquisition represents a transformational moment for G2 and, more importantly, the global B2B software industry," said Godard Abel, CEO and co-founder of G2. "By integrating the verified reviews, insights, and audiences from Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp, we're building the trusted data foundation for buyers and sellers of software for the age of AI."

Uniting trust, scale, and intelligence to redefine software buying.

After the acquisition, G2 plans to include the data assets and capabilities from Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp into its market-leading platform. This will help the company strengthen the search and recommendation experiences already utilizing AI technology, maximizing the overall market lead. Consequently, the combined platforms will help the companies achieve:

* Provide access to more than 6 million verified customer reviews to inform confident purchasing decisions
* Reach over 200 million annual software buyers worldwide across owned and operated properties
* Support more than 10,000 software vendors with data-driven marketing and demand generation solutions
* Cover over 2,000 software and services categories through an expanded, industry-leading taxonomy
* Deliver first- and second-party Buyer Intent data on a much larger scale

With this broadened foundation, G2 aims to help buyers, vendors, and others in its ecosystem at every phase of the software lifecycle.

Increasing the value to buyers, vendors, and partners.

Meanwhile, this acquisition for the buyer provides more insights and suggestions on AI. Additionally, with more verified reviews and feedback from users, G2.ai shall continue to evolve as the go-to source for buyers to make better software purchasing decisions as quickly as possible.

The aggregation of reach and traffic across platforms enables vendors to maximize their visibilities to pull in demand, both organic search and AI search contexts. Leveraging G2's strong AEO foundations, combined with their SEO strategy, the organization seeks to create Buyer Intent signals, advertising, and a pay-per-leads initiative on a worldwide scale.

Datasets for partners, consultants, and investors will now yield more valuable insights thanks to data from Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp. This will facilitate better integration and targeting efforts, and provide a stronger analysis to help with research, funding, and other strategies for B2B software development.

attributes.body: Capterra, the world's leading software discovery and reviews platform for small and new businesses, today announced Claire Alexander as its new General Manager. Capterra covers more than 450 categories of business software. Alexander brings nearly two decades of experience in digital strategy, new product development, and go-to-market leadership across the media, clean tech, education tech and advertising tech industries. At Capterra, she will oversee all day-to-day operations and lead the strategic vision for the organization. "We know that choosing the right technology can be a game-changer for organizations of any size," said Alexander. Alexander joins Capterra from Oracle USA, where she was responsible for monetizing the raw data assets held by the Oracle Data Cloud. She joined Oracle through the acquisition of AddThis, where she served as Vice President of Marketing. Founded in 1999, Capterra was acquired in 2015 by Gartner, Inc.
